title: A Working Republic and Its Discontents
partB: The peaceful transfer of power from the Federalists to Jefferson's Republicans after the election of 1800, the first between parties in the republic's history.
The 1823 declaration that the American continents were closed to new European colonization and that European interference in them would be viewed as a threat to the United States.
Jackson's practice of filling federal offices with his party's supporters, defended as rotation in office and attacked as corruption.
The textile arrangement at Lowell, where young women lived in company boardinghouses, worked set hours, and were held to strict rules of conduct.
Jefferson's 1807 ban on American exports, meant to pressure Britain and France to respect American rights without going to war.
The document issued at Seneca Falls in 1848 that rewrote the Declaration of Independence to charge men with the subjection of women.
Washington's 1796 valedictory, warning against permanent foreign alliances and the spirit of party.
The House rule, renewed session after session from 1836, that tabled antislavery petitions automatically and without debate.
